dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4401.text: To gather. Formed from 禾, with 責 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4402.text: To pile up. Formed from 禾, with 失 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Pile it up in orderly heaps.”

shuowen:4403.text: To bind into bundles. Formed from 禾, with 囷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4404.text: Fine grain. Formed from 禾, with 果 indicating the sound. Another explanation: grain without husks.

shuowen:4405.text: To pound grain without soaking it. Formed from 禾, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4406.text: Defined as 𥞸, apparently a kind or preparation of grain; the precise gloss is uncertain. Formed from 禾, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4407.text: Grain husk, 𥢶. Formed from 禾, with 孚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4408.text: Bran. Formed from 禾, with 會 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4409.text: Grain husks. Formed from 禾 and 米, with 庚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4410.text: The husk of grain. Formed from 禾, with 羔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4411.text: Grain straw stripped of its outer skin, used as a mat in sacrifices to Heaven. Formed from 禾, with 皆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4412.text: Grain stalks. Formed from 禾, with 旱 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Someone threw in a bundle of straw.”

shuowen:4413.text: Grain stalks. Formed from 禾, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4414.text: Grain that has not filled out. Formed from 禾, with 比 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4415.text: Wheat stalks. Formed from 禾, with 肙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4416.text: Millet stalks. Formed from 禾, with 𠛱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4417.text: Millet stalks after processing. Formed from 禾, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4418.text: Grain stalks or straw, described as 禾若秧穰; the wording is uncertain. Formed from 禾, with 央 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4419.text: 䅭䅣, a cereal name. Formed from 禾, with 㫄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4420.text: The cereal 䅭䅣. Formed from 禾, with 皇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4421.text: Grain ripening. Formed from 禾, with 千 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “A great harvest.”

shuowen:4422.text: To continue: the general name for all grains. Formed from 禾, with 𣪊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4423.text: Grain ripening. Formed from 禾, with 念 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Seldom does it fail to take five harvests.”

shuowen:4424.text: A levy on fields. Formed from 禾, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4425.text: A levy or rent. Formed from 禾, with 兌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4426.text: A cereal. Formed from 禾, with 道 indicating the sound. Sima Xiangru says: “䆃 has six ears on one stalk.”

shuowen:4427.text: Empty, without food. Formed from 禾, with 荒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4428.text: To grasp and take grain stalks. Formed from 禾, with 魚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4429.text: Things emerging gradually. Formed from 禾, with 肖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4430.text: Cereal grains ripening. Formed from 禾, with abbreviated 𤒅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4431.text: The state enfeoffed to Boyi’s descendants. Its land suits grain. Formed from 禾 and abbreviated 舂. Another explanation: 秦 is a cereal name.

shuowen:4432.text: To weigh or assess. Formed from 禾, with 爯 indicating the sound. Grain grows at the spring equinox. At the summer solstice the sun’s shadow can be measured. Grain has awns, which become fixed at the autumn equinox. In pitch-pipe measurement, twelve awns equal one fen; ten fen make one cun. By weight, twelve grains make one fen, and twelve fen one zhu. Thus all standards and measures follow 禾.

shuowen:4433.text: A standard. Formed from 禾 and 斗; 斗 means measuring.

shuowen:4434.text: A measure or grade. Ten hairs make one cheng; ten cheng make one fen; ten fen make one cun. Formed from 禾, with 呈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4435.text: Eighty threads of cloth make a 稯. Formed from 禾, with 㚇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4436.text: Five 稯 make a 秭. Formed from 禾, with 𠂔 indicating the sound. Another explanation: counting 億 up to ten thousand gives 秭.

shuowen:4437.text: Two 秭 make a 秅. Formed from 禾, with 乇 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Two hundred forty jin make a bing; four bing a ju; ten ju a zong; ten zong a cha. Four hundred bing make one cha.”

shuowen:4438.text: One hundred twenty jin. One 䄷 of rice yields twenty sheng of grain; one 䄷 of cereal or millet yields sixteen and two-thirds sheng. Formed from 禾, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4439.text: The return of its season. Formed from 禾, with 其 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “A cycle of three hundred and sixty days.”

shuowen:4440.text: Grain gathered for threshing. Another explanation: settled or secure. Formed from 禾 and abbreviated 隱. Ancient writing also used 安隱.

shuowen:4441.text: To bundle stalks. Formed from 禾, with 𦎫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4442.text: Suitably spaced and sparse. Formed from two 禾. All characters in this group are formed from 秝. Read like 歷.

shuowen:4443.text: To combine. Formed from 又 holding 秝: 兼 holds two grain stalks, while 秉 holds one.

shuowen:4444.text: A sticky cereal. Planted at the great heat, hence called 黍. Formed from 禾, with abbreviated 雨 indicating the sound. Confucius says: “Millet can make wine: grain entering water.” All characters in this group are formed from 黍.

shuowen:4445.text: The cereal 穄. Formed from 黍, with 麻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4446.text: A kind of millet. Formed from 黍, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4447.text: To stick to one another. Formed from 黍, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4448.text: Sticky. Formed from 黍, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4449.text: Sticky. Formed from 黍, with 日 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “What is unrighteous does not hold together.”

shuowen:4450.text: Shoe adhesive. Formed from 黍, with abbreviated 𥝢 indicating the sound; 𥝢 is ancient-script 利. Shoe adhesive is made with millet grain.

shuowen:4451.text: To process the decayed lower leaves of millet, cereals and beans. Formed from 黍, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4452.text: Fragrant. Formed from 黍 and 甘. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The millet and grain are fragrant.” All characters in this group are formed from 香.

shuowen:4453.text: Fragrance perceptible from afar. Formed from 香, with 殸 indicating the sound; 殸 is large-seal 磬.

shuowen:4454.text: A rich fragrance. Formed from 香, with 复 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4455.text: Grain kernels. Depicts the kernels of grain. All characters in this group are formed from 米.

shuowen:4456.text: A grain name. Formed from 米, with abbreviated 梁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4457.text: To harvest grain early. Formed from 米, with 焦 indicating the sound. Another explanation: small.

shuowen:4458.text: Rice weighing one 䄷 yields twenty dou of unhusked grain; if it yields ten dou of milled grain it is called 毇; if six and two-thirds dou, 粲. Formed from 米, with 𣦼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4459.text: Unhusked grain weighing one 䄷 measures sixteen and two-thirds dou; pounded to one hu of milled grain, it is called 䊪. Formed from 米, with 萬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4460.text: To select. Formed from 米, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4461.text: Finely milled grain, 毇. Formed from 米, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4462.text: Coarse or sparse. Formed from 米, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4463.text: Poor grain. Formed from 米, with 北 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou has a “䉾 Oath.”

shuowen:4464.text: Sprouted grain. Formed from 米, with 辥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4465.text: Rice mixed into soup, 糂. Formed from 米, with 立 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4466.text: Soaked or broken-down grain. Formed from 米, with 睪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4467.text: To mix grain into soup. Another explanation: a grain, 粒. Formed from 米, with 甚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4468.text: A rice preparation made by cooking, called 糪; the recorded wording 炊，米者 is incomplete. Formed from 米, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4469.text: Grain soup or porridge, 糝. Formed from 米, with 麻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4470.text: Mixed porridge. Formed from 米, with 覃 indicating the sound. Read like 𨝸.

shuowen:4471.text: Soaked grain. Formed from 米, with 尼 indicating the sound. Jiaozhi has 𥹆泠 County.

shuowen:4472.text: The starter for brewing wine. Formed from 米, with abbreviated 𥷚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4473.text: Wine dregs. Formed from 米, with 曹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4474.text: Dry. Formed from 米, with 𤰈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4475.text: Roasted rice and wheat. Formed from 米, with 臭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4476.text: To pound roasted grain. Formed from 臼 and 米.

shuowen:4477.text: Provisions. Formed from 米, with 胥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4478.text: Grain. Formed from 米, with 量 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4479.text: Mixed cooked grain. Formed from 米, with 丑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4480.text: Grain. Formed from 米, with 翟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4481.text: Bran. Formed from 米, with 蔑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4482.text: Unmixed. Formed from 米, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4483.text: To supply guests with fodder and grain. Formed from 米, with 气 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The men of Qi came to provision the feudal lords.”

shuowen:4484.text: Stale, foul-smelling grain. Formed from 米, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4485.text: Something applied to the face. Formed from 米, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4486.text: Powder. Formed from 米, with 卷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4487.text: Scattering, 𥻦. Formed from 米, with 悉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4488.text: 䊝𥻦, to scatter it. Formed from 米, with 殺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4489.text: Crushed or broken. Formed from 米, with 靡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4490.text: Theft originating within is called 竊. Formed from 穴 and 米; both 𥜽 and 廿 indicate the sound. 廿 is ancient-script 疾; 𥜽 is ancient-script 偰.

shuowen:4491.text: Grain for food. Formed from 米, with 長 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4492.text: 糟粕, wine dregs. Formed from 米, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4493.text: 粔籹, rings fried in fat. Formed from 米, with 巨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4494.text: The fried food 粔籹. Formed from 米, with 女 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4495.text: Grain wrapped in reed leaves. Formed from 米, with 㚇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4496.text: Malt syrup. Formed from 米, with 唐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4497.text: One hu of grain pounded down to eight dou. Formed from 䊆 and 殳. All characters in this group are formed from 毇.

shuowen:4498.text: One hu of 䊪 grain pounded down to nine dou is 糳. Formed from 毇, with 丵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4499.text: To pound. Ancient people dug a mortar into the ground; later they hollowed wood or stone. Pictographic; the middle represents grain. All characters in this group are formed from 臼.

shuowen:4500.text: To pound grain. Formed from 廾 holding a pestle over 臼; 午 is abbreviated 杵. In antiquity Yongfu first devised grain-pounding.
